queries.query: Louhi's bargain: her daughter in marriage to whoever can forge her the Sampo with its many-colored cover out of a feather, a barley grain, and a wisp of wool
queries.note: 'Tips of white-swan feathers', 'milk of greatest virtue', 'finest wool of lambkins', 'hammer me the lid in colors' compressed and paraphrased; 'Louhi' and 'Sampo' kept as names every reader knows.

queries.query: Lemminkainen's mother rakes the river of Tuoni for the scattered pieces of her son and joins them back into a living man
queries.note: The restoration in Rune XV; 'half the head, a fore-arm', 'flesh to flesh with skill she places' paraphrased; the raven's advice to leave him as a sea-beast dropped.

queries.query: swallowed whole by the sleeping giant Wipunen, Wainamoinen torments him from inside his body until the ancient words of origin are given up
queries.note: The lost-words episode; the boat built from a knife handle and the rowing 'through every gland and vessel' paraphrased to torment from inside; both names kept.

queries.query: the herd-boy Kullervo avenges the hostess's malice by singing wolves and bears into the shape of cattle and driving them home to the smith's wife at milking time
queries.note: The raven's counsel and the death of Ilmarinen's wife; 'drive them home like spotted cattle', 'sing the forest wolves together' paraphrased; 'Kullervo' kept — the cycle bears his name.

queries.query: why does knowing the origin of a thing give power to heal or control it
queries.note: The origin of iron recited to close Wainamoinen's wound, the balsam tested on broken stone; word-power over origins is answered by many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: what happens to the world when the sun and moon are stolen away and hidden
queries.note: Louhi hides sun and moon in the stone mountain; the hidden-luminaries motif recurs across traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
